title: Command Palette Dock requires PowerToys restart to detect a newly connected monitor

judgment.rationale: Current main already contains a Command Palette Dock topology-change fix that matches the hot-plug and resume symptoms in this report.
evidence: The issue describes the Dock failing to appear on a newly connected monitor until PowerToys is restarted.
Two follow-up comments confirm the same monitor-reconnect and monitor-wake behavior.

Recent current-main history includes “CmdPal: Fix Command Palette Dock breaking on monitor topology changes” (#49814), which explicitly calls out docking, undocking, Win+P, and empty or missing docks.
judgment.recommended_action: Link the handled-by-main Command Palette Dock topology fix instead of creating a new design for the same hot-plug monitor bug.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reported monitor-topology bug is already covered by a merged current-main fix for Dock topology changes.

issue_context.summary: The report says Command Palette Dock only recognizes a newly connected monitor after restarting PowerToys, and current main already contains a Dock topology-change fix that matches that failure mode closely.
known_information: The body gives a precise current-build repro for connecting a monitor after PowerToys startup and seeing Dock fail to appear on the configured display.
Two commenters independently report the same behavior after dock reconnect or monitor sleep/wake.
The issue includes a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP and is labeled Product-Command Palette.
inferences: This is a stale-monitor-topology problem inside Command Palette Dock rather than a Windows display-detection problem, because Windows sees the display and PowerToys begins working again after restart.
The current-main topology-change fix is likely the intended resolution path for this issue rather than a separate unfixed bug.
issue_context.analysis: Because the issue has not changed and current main now contains a fix whose scope explicitly matches the report, the lightweight revalidation should treat this as handled-by-fix evidence, not as a request for another design. The maintainer-facing action is to point at the merged fix and verify it against a build newer than 0.100.2.
initial_investigation: src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Services/MonitorService.cs now caches monitor snapshots and exposes NotifyMonitorsChanged().
src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/MainWindow.xaml.cs forwards WM_DISPLAYCHANGE to MonitorService so the monitor list is refreshed even when no Dock window is visible.
The merged PR #49814 adds retries for stable monitor IDs, debounces topology changes, and documents exactly the empty/missing Dock behavior described in this issue.

actions.label: Link dock topology fix

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed repro and the follow-up confirmations. Current main now has a targeted Dock topology-change fix in #49814 that refreshes monitor IDs on WM_DISPLAYCHANGE, retries transient monitor-ID lookups, and debounces monitor-topology writes. This report was filed against 0.100.2 before that merge, so the next maintainer step is to verify it against a build that includes #49814 and then close it as handled if the repro is gone.
